title: Tardigrade Isolation and Phylogenetic Characterization Protocol
author: Tom D'Elia
materials: Gather materials required to collect Tardigrades from environmental samples. Lab notebook Petri dish or shallow clear container Razor blade or pocket knife Pen or marker GPS enabled device

Guidelines: Make sure all materials are sterilized ahead of time. Materials: 1.5 mL microcentrifuge tubes 50% Ethanol Invitrogen™ UltraPure™ DNase/RNase-Free Distilled Water Thermo Fisher Scientific Catalog #10-977-015 Invitrogen UltraPure DNase/RNase-Free Distilled Water (ThermoFisher) Fisherbrand™ Pellet Pestles™ (Pestles with microcentrifuge tubes, Thermo Fisher Scientific, 12-141-367, Resuspend protein and DNA pellets or grind soft tissue in microcentrifuge tubes, https://www.fishersci.com/shop/products ) Pestles GeneJET Genomic DNA Purification Kit Thermo Fisher Catalog #K0721 GeneJET Genomic DNA Purification Kit (ThermoFisher)

The free bioinformatics software MEGA can be used to complete the phylogenetic analysis of the DNA sequences prepared in DNA Subway and the sequences collected from the BLAST results. We recommend MEGA version 7 to allow easy editing of the tree in PowerPoint. The general workflow is to generate a multiple sequence alignment of all of the DNA sequences and construct a phylogenetic tree.

steps.title: Collect moss/lichen sample
steps.instruction: Find a lichen or moss growing on any substrate (trees, mulch beds, decaying wood, shaded rocks or brick walls), take photographs, and record date, temperature, rain/moisture level, height, GPS coordinates, substrate type, and visual description of the sample.

steps.title: Transfer sample to petri dish and label
steps.instruction: Hold a petri dish under the sample and scrape enough material to cover a quarter to half of the dish, close the dish, and label it with your name, a sample number (e.g., Moss 1 or Lichen 1), and the collection date using a permanent marker; also record all metadata in a lab notebook.

steps.title: Store sample refrigerated
steps.instruction: Place the closed petri dish in a refrigerator at 4 °C until you are ready to rehydrate and isolate tardigrades.

steps.title: Rehydrate sample (soak)
steps.instruction: Add deionized (DI) water to the petri dish enough to submerge the sample (full coverage not required).

substeps.instruction: Incubate at 37 °C for 5–10 min, gently stir, then observe for tardigrades; re‑incubate for another 10 min at 37 °C and repeat until tardigrades become visible.
Alternatively, soak at room temperature and check periodically (hourly or every 24 h).

steps.title: Microscopic examination for tardigrades
steps.instruction: Using a light microscope, first scan the dish with a 4X objective (40× total) moving slowly to avoid water sloshing, focusing especially near moss/lichen fragments; then switch to a 10X objective (100× total) to observe movement and identify tardigrades, rotifers, nematodes, moss mites, amoebas, paramecia, etc., and record the number of tardigrades observed.

steps.title: Assign IDs and photograph tardigrades
steps.instruction: Give each observed tardigrade a unique identifier (e.g., Moss 1‑Tardigrade 1 or Lichen 4‑Tardigrade 18), take several photographs for later identification, and note the identifier, sample number, and count in your notebook.

steps.title: Isolate individual tardigrades
steps.instruction: Using a Pasteur pipette, collect one tardigrade at a time while viewing at 40×, pulling up less than 100 µL of water (avoid drawing water into the bulb), and immediately squirt the water and tardigrade into a labeled 1.5 mL microcentrifuge tube (label includes sample type, sample number, tardigrade number, and date).

steps.title: Store isolated tardigrades
steps.instruction: Place the labeled microcentrifuge tubes in a refrigerated rack at 4 °C; tubes remain stable for weeks to months until DNA extraction.

steps.title: Prepare for DNA extraction
steps.instruction: Ensure each tube contains less than 100 µL of water; if excess water is present, remove it carefully without losing the tardigrade, then grind the tardigrade with a sterile pestle inside the tube.

steps.title: Add digestion solution and proteinase K
steps.instruction: Add 180 µL of Digestion Solution and 20 µL of Proteinase K Solution to the tube, then vortex or pipette up and down to obtain a homogeneous suspension; if a pestle was used, spin it in the solution to release all tissue.

steps.title: Incubate lysate at 56 °C
steps.instruction: Incubate the tube at 56 °C until the tardigrade is completely lysed (minimum 1 hour for samples <5 mg), vortexing the tube occasionally during incubation.

steps.title: Add RNase A and incubate
steps.instruction: Add 20 µL of RNase A Solution, vortex, and incubate for 10 minutes (00:10:00) at room temperature.

steps.title: Add lysis solution
steps.instruction: Add 200 µL of Lysis Solution, vortex thoroughly for 15 seconds (00:00:15) until the mixture is homogeneous.

steps.title: Add ethanol
steps.instruction: Add 400 µL of 50 % ethanol and mix by vortexing or pipetting up and down.

steps.title: Bind lysate to column (wash 1)
steps.instruction: Transfer the entire lysate to a GeneJET Genomic DNA Purification Column placed in a collection tube and centrifuge for 1 minute (00:01:00) at 6000 × g; discard the flow‑through and place the column into a new 2 mL collection tube.

steps.title: Wash column with Buffer I
steps.instruction: Add 500 µL of Wash Buffer I (with ethanol), centrifuge for 1 minute at 8000 × g, discard the flow‑through, and return the column to the collection tube.

steps.title: Wash column with Buffer II
steps.instruction: Add 500 µL of Wash Buffer II (with ethanol), centrifuge for 3 minutes (00:03:00) at ≥12000 × g; if residual liquid remains, perform an additional spin for 1 minute at maximum speed and discard the flow‑through.

steps.title: Elute genomic DNA
steps.instruction: Place the column in a sterile 1.5 mL microcentrifuge tube, add 30 µL of sterile Invitrogen UltraPure DNase/RNase‑Free Distilled Water to the membrane center, incubate 2 minutes (00:02:00) at room temperature, then centrifuge 1 minute at 8000 × g to collect the eluate.

steps.title: Store or use purified DNA
steps.instruction: Use the DNA immediately for downstream applications or store it at –20 °C.

steps.title: Prepare PCR master mix
steps.instruction: For each reaction, combine 12.5 µL Promega Green GoTaq, 0.5 µL forward primer (10 µM), 0.5 µL reverse primer (10 µM), and 12.5 µL sterile water; multiply the total volume by the number of samples plus two extra reactions for pipetting error.

steps.title: Set up PCR reactions
steps.instruction: Dispense 24 µL of the master mix into each 0.2 µL PCR tube, then add 1 µL of the tardigrade DNA template to the corresponding tube.

steps.title: Run PCR program
steps.instruction: Program the thermocycler as follows: 95 °C for 1 min; 95 °C for 1 min; 60 °C for 1 min 30 sec; 72 °C for 1 min 30 sec; repeat steps 2‑4 a total of 35 cycles; final extension at 72 °C for 7 min.

steps.title: Prepare 1 % agarose gel
steps.instruction: In a 250 mL Erlenmeyer flask, dissolve 0.4 g agarose in 40 mL 1× TAE (40 mM Tris‑acetate, 1 mM EDTA, pH 8.3) to make a 1 % gel; add 4 µL SYBR Safe dye, microwave until fully dissolved, and stir periodically to prevent boiling over.

steps.title: Run gel electrophoresis
steps.instruction: Load 10‑15 µL of each PCR product directly (no loading dye) into the gel, include an appropriate DNA ladder, run at 100 V for 45 minutes (00:45:00), then visualize bands under UV light, photograph, and record band intensity and size (expected ~1300 bp).

steps.title: Prepare PCR products for sequencing
steps.instruction: Dilute PCR products that show strong bands 1:1 with sterile water; do not dilute products with faint bands before sending for Sanger sequencing (forward and reverse primers submitted separately).

steps.title: Process sequences in DNA Subway
steps.instruction: Log in as a Guest at https://dnasubway.cyverse.org/, select the Blue Route → Phylogenetics DNA, upload the forward and reverse AB1 files, then sequentially use Sequence Viewer, Sequence Trimmer (remove Ns), Pair Builder (reverse‑complement and pair), and Consensus Builder to generate a consensus sequence.

steps.title: BLAST consensus sequences
steps.instruction: Select the consensus sequence, click BLASTN (either within DNA Subway or on NCBI), run the search, and record matches with >85 % query coverage, noting accession numbers, scientific names, collection locations, years, and any associated publications.

steps.title: Collect top BLAST hits in FASTA
steps.instruction: For each chosen hit (3‑5 per sample), click the accession number, go to the GenBank Nucleotide page, click FASTA, and copy the entire FASTA entry (including the ‘>’ header) into a text file.

steps.title: Multiple sequence alignment in MEGA
steps.instruction: Open MEGA, choose Align → Edit/Build → Create new alignment → DNA, paste all FASTA sequences, then Align → ClustalW or Muscle (default settings); after alignment, remove any unusually short sequences and replace them with longer conspecific sequences if available.

steps.title: Construct neighbor‑joining tree in MEGA
steps.instruction: From the main MEGA window select Data → Phylogenetic Analysis, answer “No” to protein‑coding nucleotides, then Phylogeny → Construct/Test Neighbor‑Joining Tree…, choose “Yes” to use active data, set Test of Phylogeny to Bootstrap with 1000 replications, leave other settings default, and click Compute to generate the tree.

steps.title: Edit phylogenetic tree in PowerPoint
steps.instruction: In MEGA, copy the tree image (Image → Copy to Clipboard), paste into a blank PowerPoint slide, right‑click the image, choose “Edit Picture” and confirm conversion to a Microsoft Office drawing; then edit taxon names, font colors, and line weights as desired, and save the edited figure for presentation.
